notes: Engraved marble plaque by a doorway of the Armenian Cilicia primary school in Aleppo, flash photo. Arabic year in Arabic-Indic digits (١٩٢١) to the left of تأسست on the same row; Armenian line year in Western digits. Western Armenian classical orthography (ԵԱ).

author: Alen Ištoković

notes: Weathered wooden board with metal letters on a dead tree beside the Palmyra–Baghdad desert highway (Bagdad Cafe 66, near Palmyra). Round '66' plate hangs below; a small '66' sign further down the road is a distractor. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: twiga_swala

notes: Small marble plaque beside the arched doorway of Beit Ghazaleh (Aleppo old city), small in frame. A small Arabic subtitle line (century of construction) and '17th C.A.D' below are too small to transcribe reliably and are left out. House number plate '12' at right is a distractor.

author: Alen Ištoković
attribution: Photo: Alen Ištoković, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Arabic_signs_-_panoramio.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Cluster of four lawyers' arrow signs on a lamp post in Deir ez-Zor; the target is the right-middle black sign (left arrow). Distractors: 'المحامي خير الله عبد الجبار الدخيل' (white, top right), 'المحامي سليمان خليل عبود' (black, top left) and 'المحامي عادل غسان الحمود' (lower left), whose small address lines are not legible. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Bernard Gagnon
attribution: Photo: Bernard Gagnon, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Street_sign_in_Damascus_01.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Blue enamel Damascus street plate near the Umayyad Mosque: main panel (lane name, Latin transliteration, French 'Cul-de-sac' and code) then the left panels (district 07 Old Damascus, quarter 3 al-Hamidiyya). Decorative kashida stretches in حارة, الجقمقية and الحميدية are omitted. Small chips/black marks on 'AL-JAQ' and between 'sac' and '012001' are damage, not text. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

lines.latin: tabib baytari mujaz min Faransa (veterinarian licensed in France)

notes: Old enamel/painted name plate of a veterinarian's house in Damascus, frontal. 'Dr' is written with a small raised, underlined r; 'الدكتور' is faded compared with the bright red 'منزل'. Arabic third line says 'licensed from France' while the English says 'From Paris'.

author: Bernard Gagnon
attribution: Photo: Bernard Gagnon, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Azem_Palace_01.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.

lines.text: بناه والي دمشق أسعد باشا العظم
lines.latin: Banahu wali Dimashq As'ad Basha al-'Azm (Built by the governor of Damascus As'ad Pasha al-Azm)

lines.text: BATIE PAR LE GOUVERNEUR DE DAMAS

notes: Engraved marble plaque at the entrance of the Azem Palace, Damascus. Small sukun/vowel marks over قصر العظم and a fatha on سنة are not transcribed; Arabic-Indic digits for the dates. The ‘ in AS‘AD and AL-‘AZEM is an ayn mark (left single quote). The brown tourist tile at right repeats 'قصر العظم / A'zem Palace' (with EU/municipal logos) and is a matching secondary sign. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: jemasmith
attribution: Photo: jemasmith, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/26085795@N02/4706162958. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Arrow-shaped cream directional sign (pointing left) hanging among scarves and clothes in a souk stall, Old Damascus; red Arabic over black Latin. Final ى of 'مقهى' undotted. The sign is mid-frame and small relative to the cluttered scene; a partial green sign at the lower left edge is a distractor.

author: upyernoz
attribution: Photo: upyernoz, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/48600082269@N01/48703787. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Boulos sweet shop / bakery in Aleppo, at night. Raised Arabic letters over the left arch; vertical lettering 'YEAR 1876' and 'BOULOS' on the brick pillar (read top to bottom, the final S partly faded); cursive 'Boulos' over the right arch. A second faint 'Boulos' at the far right edge is a distractor.

author: Bernard Gagnon

notes: Blue distance sign near Tall Aqibrin in the Aleppo countryside; red route shields '6' (square) and '06' (diamond) at the bottom. The Arabic distance is in Arabic-Indic digits (٤٠). Orange chevron at right is a distractor. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

lines.latin: banaha as-Sultan Sulayman al-Qanuni (built by Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent)

notes: Engraved marble heritage plaque (Takiyya Sulaymaniyya complex, Damascus), frontal and sharp. Arabic line 1 carries partial vowel marks (fatha/damma/sukun/shadda) that are omitted here; the hijri 'هـ' and 'م' after the years are small raised letters; years use Arabic-Indic digits. The final H of 'SULAYMANIYYAH' has a small mark under it (transliteration diacritic). 'I' in 'SULAYMAN I' is a serifed Roman numeral. A shadow covers the left edge but no text is lost.
derivative: Flickr's published 1024 px 'large' rendition, served by the Openverse image API (Flickr originals were throttled for this client)
